issues.legal_issue: A delegated rule cannot impose a filing deadline for invoking a revisional power that the governing statute allows to be exercised at any time.
material_facts: The statute authorized the revisional authority to call for the record of a proceeding at any time to examine the legality or propriety of an order.
The challenged rule required a revision petition to be filed within the period prescribed for an appeal, which was thirty days.
The statute specified time limits for appeals and for certain applications, but did not authorize rule-making to prescribe a time limit for revision petitions.
issues.conclusion: The rule was ultra vires the statute insofar as it imposed a time limit for filing revision petitions.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 24, the revisional authority may act at any time. Sections 22 and 23 prescribe time limits for appeals, while section 40(2)(a) expressly permits rules to prescribe the time for certain applications. Section 40(2)(l), concerning appeals and applications for review or revision, authorizes rules about form, manner and procedure but omits authority to prescribe time limits. The general rule-making power in section 40(1) cannot support a rule that conflicts with the Act; a rule cannot override the statute. No earlier cases are relied on.

rule.if: revision_limitation_challenged_in_writ and statute_allows_revision_at_any_time and rule_imposes_fixed_revision_filing_period and delegated_rulemaking_power_omits_authority_to_set_revision_deadline

predicates.revision_limitation_challenged_in_writ: A party challenges in a writ proceeding a rule that limits the time for seeking revision.
predicates.statute_allows_revision_at_any_time: The governing statute authorizes the revisional authority to act at any time.
predicates.rule_imposes_fixed_revision_filing_perio: The rule requires a revision petition to be filed within a fixed period.
predicates.delegated_rulemaking_power_omits_authori: The statute's grant of rule-making authority does not authorize rules to set a deadline for revision petitions.

issues.definition: When a rule imposing a fixed filing period for revision is challenged in a writ proceeding, and the statute permits revision at any time without authorizing rule-makers to set such a deadline, the deadline rule is invalid.

issues.legal_issue: An order rejecting a revision solely as time-barred under an invalid filing deadline, and an order merely affirming that rejection without addressing the challenge, cannot stand.
material_facts: The revision petition was dismissed solely because it was considered out of time under the rule's filing deadline.
The merits of the revision petition were not considered, and the dismissal was not based on laches.
The reviewing government authority merely affirmed the dismissal and did not address the contention raised or give reasons.
The court held that no statutory limitation period applied to invoking the revisional jurisdiction.
issues.conclusion: The dismissal of the revision and the order affirming it were set aside, and the matter was remanded for disposal in accordance with law.
issues.legal_principle: Because the statutory revisional power could be invoked at any time and the rule could not impose a filing deadline, rejecting the revision solely as time-barred involved an error of law apparent on the face of the record. The order that merely affirmed that rejection without dealing with the contention also could not stand. The court relied on section 24 and its conclusion that rule 104(1) was ultra vires; no earlier cases are relied on.

rule.if: writ_review_of_administrative_orders and revision_rejected_only_as_untimely and revision_filing_deadline_rule_invalid and reviewing_order_only_affirms_without_addressing_the_challenge

predicates.writ_review_of_administrative_orders: A party seeks writ review of administrative orders concerning a revision proceeding.
predicates.revision_rejected_only_as_untimely: The revision was rejected solely because it was treated as filed out of time, without consideration of its merits or a finding of laches.
predicates.revision_filing_deadline_rule_invalid: The filing deadline applied to the revision is invalid because it conflicts with the governing statute.
predicates.reviewing_order_only_affirms_without_add: A reviewing authority merely affirms the rejection without addressing the contention against the filing deadline.

issues.definition: When writ review concerns a revision rejected solely under an invalid deadline and the reviewing authority merely affirms without addressing the challenge, the orders are set aside and the matter is remanded.

issues.legal_issue: A partner is competent to represent a partnership firm in a revision proceeding.
material_facts: The revision proceeding concerned a partnership firm.
A partner of the firm acted as its representative.
issues.conclusion: A partner of a firm is competent to represent the firm.
issues.legal_principle: The court stated that a partner of a firm is competent to represent it. No statutory provision or earlier case is relied on for this statement.

predicates.revision_proceeding_involves_partnership: The proceeding concerns a partnership firm.
predicates.representative_is_partner_of_firm: The person representing the firm is one of its partners.

issues.definition: When a revision proceeding concerns a partnership firm and its representative is a partner, the partner may represent the firm.
